## How Muslims see Jesus (peace be upon him)

Muslims love and honour Jesus, ʿĪsā ibn Maryam ("Jesus, son of Mary"), as one of the greatest prophets and messengers of God. Believing in him is part of a Muslim's faith.

- **The Messiah, and a Word from God.** The Quran mentions Jesus by name about 25 times. It calls him al-Masīḥ (the Messiah) and "a Word from God" (Quran 3:45).
- **A miraculous birth.** He was born to the Virgin Mary without a father. Mary is one of the most honoured women in Islam, and a whole chapter of the Quran, Surah Maryam, is named after her (Quran 19:16–34).
- **Miracles by God's permission.** He spoke as a baby in the cradle, healed the blind and the lepers, and raised the dead, all by God's permission (Quran 5:110).
- **A human messenger, not God.** Like Adam, he was created by God's command "Be" (Quran 3:59). He called people to worship the One God alone.
- **Not crucified, but raised up by God.** Muslims believe he was not killed or crucified. God raised him up (Quran 4:157–158).
- **He will return.** Muslims believe Jesus will come back before the Day of Judgment to restore justice.
- **Good news of a messenger to come.** He gave good news of a messenger who would come after him (Quran 61:6).

This is why Muslims say "peace be upon him" whenever they mention his name.
